question.explanation:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

\begin{align} \int _{1}^2 \left[ \int_{0}^1 \dfrac {e^{2x}\, \textrm d x}{y} \right] \textrm dy &= \int _{1}^2 \dfrac {1}{y} \left[ \int_{0}^1 e^{2x}\,\textrm d x \right] \textrm dy \\[5pt] & = \int_{1}^2 \dfrac{1}{y} \left[\dfrac{e^{2x}}{2} \right]_{0}^{1} \, \textrm dy \\[5pt] & = \int _{1}^2 \dfrac{1}{y} \left( \dfrac{e^{2}}{2} - \dfrac {e^{0}}{2}\right) \textrm dy \\[5pt] & = \int _{1}^2 \dfrac {e^{2}-1}{2y} \, \textrm dy \\[5pt] \end{align}

Then, we integrate with respect to $y\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} \int _{1}^2 \dfrac {e^{2}-1}{2y} \, \textrm dy &= \dfrac{e^{2}-1}{2} \int _{1}^2 \dfrac{\textrm dy}{y} \\[5pt] & = \left[ \dfrac {e^2-1}2 \ln |y| \right]_{1}^2 \\[5pt] & = \dfrac {e^2-1}2 (\ln 2 - \ln 1) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac {\ln 2(e^2-1)}2 \end{align}

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

\begin{align} \int _3^4\left[ \int_{0}^4 (5^{y-3}\sqrt{x})\, \textrm d x \right] \textrm dy & =\int _3^4 5^{y-3}\left[ \int_{0}^4 \sqrt{x}\, \textrm d x \right] \textrm dy\\[5pt] & =\int _3^4 5^{y-3} \left[ \dfrac{2}{3}\left(\sqrt{x}\right)^3 \right]_{0}^{4} \, \textrm dy \\[5pt] & =\int _3^4 5^{y-3}\left( \dfrac{2}{3}\left(\sqrt{4}\right)^3 - \dfrac{2}{3}\left(\sqrt{0}\right)^3 \right)\, \textrm dy \\[5pt] & =\int _3^4 \dfrac{16 \cdot 5^{y-3}}{3}\, \textrm dy \end{align}

Then, we integrate with respect to $y\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} \int _3^4 \dfrac{16 \cdot 5^{y-3}}{3}\, \textrm dy & = \dfrac{16}{3}\left[ \dfrac{5^{y-3}}{\ln 5} \right]_3^4\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{16}{3}\left(\dfrac{5^{4-3}}{\ln{5}} - \dfrac{5^{3-3}}{\ln{5}} \right)\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{16}{3}\left(\dfrac{5-1}{\ln{5}} \right)\\[5pt] & = \dfrac {64}{3\ln 5} \end{align}

exampleAnswers.title: Evaluating a Double Integral Over a Rectangular Domain

question.text: Evaluate the double integral $\displaystyle \iint \limits_{D} (x^2+y^2) \, \textrm d A,$ where $D=\left\{ (x,y) \: : \:-1 \leq x \leq 1, \: 0 \leq y \leq 2\right\}.$
question.explanation:
First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:

\begin{align} \iint \limits_{D} (x^2+y^2)\, \textrm d A & = \int _{0}^2 \left[\int_{-1}^{1} (x^2+y^2)\, \textrm d x\right] \textrm dy \end{align}

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

\begin{align} \int _{0}^2 \left[\int_{-1}^{ 1} (x^2+y^2)\, \textrm d x\right] \textrm dy & =\int _{0}^2 \left[\int_{-1}^{ 1} (x^2+y^2)\, \textrm d x\right] \textrm dy\\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^2 \left[\dfrac{x^3}{3} +xy^2 \right]_{-1}^{1} \textrm dy \\[5pt] & = \int _{0}^2 \left[\left(\dfrac{1}{3}+ y^2\right) - \left(-\dfrac{1}{3} - y^2 \right)\right]\, \textrm dy \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^2 \left( \dfrac{2}{3} + 2y^2\right) \, \textrm dy \end{align}

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} \int_{0}^2 \left( \dfrac{2}{3} + 2y^2\right)\, \textrm dy & = \left[\dfrac{2y}{3} + \dfrac{2y^3}{3} \right]_{0}^2\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{2}{3}\left(2+2^3 - 0 \right) \\[5pt] & =\dfrac{20}{3} \end{align}

example.title: Evaluating a Double Integral Over a Rectangular Domain

question.text: Evaluate the double integral $\displaystyle \iint \limits_{D} \dfrac{y^2}{x^2+4} \, \textrm d A,$ where $D=\left\{ (x,y) \: : \:0 \leq x \leq 2, \: 0 \leq y \leq 3\right\}.$
question.explanation:
First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:

\begin{align} \iint \limits_{D} \dfrac{y^2}{x^2+4}\, \textrm d A & = \int _{0}^3 \left[\int_{0}^{ \pi/2} \dfrac{y^2}{x^2+4}\, \textrm d x\right] \textrm dy \end{align}

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

\begin{align} \int _{0}^3 \left[\int_{0}^{2} \dfrac{y^2}{x^2+4}\, \textrm d x\right] \textrm dy & =\int _{0}^3 y^2 \left[\int_{0}^{2} \dfrac{1}{x^2+4}\, \textrm d x\right] \textrm dy\\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^3 y^2\left[\dfrac{1}{2}\arctan\left( \dfrac{x}{2}\right) \right]_{0}^{2} \textrm dy \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{2} \int _{0}^3 y^2 \left(\arctan\left(1\right)-\arctan{0}\right)\, \textrm dy \\[5pt] & =\dfrac{\pi}{8} \int_{0}^3 y^2\, \textrm dy \end{align}

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} \dfrac{\pi}{8} \int_{0}^3 y^2\, \textrm dy & = \dfrac{\pi}{8}\left(\dfrac{y^3}{3} \right)\Bigg|_{0}^3\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\pi}{24}\left(3^3-0^3\right) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{9\pi}{8} \end{align}

example.title: Evaluating a Double Integral Over a Rectangular Domain

question.explanation:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant.

Making a substitution $xy=u,$ $\textrm dy = \dfrac 1 x \, \textrm du,$ we get.

\begin{align} \int_{0}^{1}\left[ \int_{0}^{1} xe^{xy} \, \textrm{d}y \right] \textrm{d}x & =\int_{0}^{1} x \left[ \int_{0}^{1} e^{xy} \, \textrm{d}y \right] \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & =\int_{0}^{1} x \left[ \int_{0}^{x} \dfrac 1 x e^{u} \, \textrm{d}u \right] \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & =\int_{0}^{1} \left[ \int_{0}^{x} e^{u} \, \textrm{d}u \right] \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{1} \big[ e^{u}\big]_{0}^{x} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{1} \left(e^{x}- 1\right) \textrm dx \end{align}

Then, we integrate with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} \int_{0}^{1} (e^{x} - 1) \, \textrm dx & = \big[ e^{x} - x \big]_{0}^{1} \\[5pt] & =\left( e - 1\right) - \left(1- 0 \right) \\[5pt] &=e - 2 \end{align}

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant:

\begin{align} \int_{\pi/4}^{\pi/2}\left[ \int_{0}^{\pi/4}2 \sin x \cos y \, \textrm{d}y \right] \textrm{d}x & =\int_{\pi/4}^{\pi/2} 2 \sin x\left[ \int_{0}^{\pi/4} \cos y \, \textrm{d}y \right] \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \int_{\pi/4}^{\pi/2} 2 \sin x \, \Big[ \sin y\Big]_{0}^{\pi/4} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] & = \int_{\pi/4}^{\pi/2} 2\sin x\cdot \left(\dfrac{\sqrt2}2-0\right) \textrm dx \\[5pt] & = \int_{\pi/4}^{\pi/2} \sqrt2 \sin x \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] \end{align}

Then, we integrate with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} \int_{\pi/4}^{\pi/2} \sqrt2 \sin x \, \textrm dx & = \sqrt2 \Big[-\cos x\Big]_{\pi/4}^{\pi/2} \\[5pt] & = \sqrt2\left(0 -\left ( -\dfrac{\sqrt2}2\right)\right) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\sqrt2^2}2\\[5pt] &=1 \end{align}
